source.title: Large-width asymptotics for ReLU neural networks with $\alpha$-Stable initializations
source.authors: S. Favaro; S. Fortini; Stefano Peluchetti

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically studies gradient-flow training of randomly initialized α-Stable ReLU networks and reports a convergence result for training loss, using a squared-error measure rather than benchmark classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an asymptotic training-loss result under explicit assumptions. It does not report CIFAR results, classification error, or experiments comparing the other claim conditions.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence of squared training loss for shallow, fully connected α-Stable ReLU networks under continuous gradient flow. This does not test V1's convolutional benchmark classification claim, V2's teacher-student local minima claim, or the comparisons and dynamics specified in V3–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' stated conclusion, but needs a technical qualification: although they call the procedure gradient descent and describe zero training error at a linear rate, their theorem analyzes continuous gradient flow and proves exponential convergence of squared training error toward zero with high probability for sufficiently large width.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes continuous gradient flow on shallow α-Stable ReLU networks with squared-error loss and linearly independent unit-norm inputs. It does not use benchmark classification experiments or the listed CIFAR recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The result is stated for α ∈ (0, 2), linearly independent unit-norm inputs, squared-error loss, and ηm = (log m)2/α.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5 bounds squared training error by its initial value times exp(−λ₀t), with probability at least 1−δ for sufficiently large width, under continuous gradient flow with ηm=(log m)^(2/α), α∈(0,2), and linearly independent unit-norm inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide shallow α-Stable ReLU networks have squared training loss converging exponentially to zero under the specified gradient-flow dynamics and input assumptions.

record.problems: The result is theoretical and conditional on linearly independent unit-norm inputs and the specified learning-rate scaling. The paper does not provide benchmark classification experiments or empirical validation of the asymptotic result.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/100; training classification error with clean, corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, frequency of spurious local minima, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh training, and normalization-free residual training.

Effects of activation-matched initialization on training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization. The initialization-distribution and kernel-limit results do not establish these comparisons.

Discrete learning rates relative to an initial stability threshold, transient loss increases, curvature changes, divergence and edge-of-stability dynamics. The continuous learning-rate scaling in R1 does not test these.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study's own theoretical result is substantive, but none of the supplied claim versions encompasses it. Its heavy-tailed initialization analysis supplies no training-speed or trainable-depth comparison for V4.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, convolutional networks, SGD or Adam, and the stated effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, depth-related training degradation, shortcuts, and the cited special recipes.
Comparisons among initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability limit, loss increases or divergence, and sharpness during training.
Batch normalization comparisons and normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: α-Stable ReLU-NN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow under squared-error loss with continuous learning rate ηm = (log m)2/α
rows.value: kY − f̃m(W(t), X; α)k₂² ≤ exp(−λ₀t)kY − f̃m(W(0), X; α)k₂²
rows.uncertainty: For every δ > 0, the result holds with probability at least 1 − δ; λ₀ > 0.
rows.note: The theorem gives an exponential upper bound on squared training error for the stated theoretical setting; it does not report finite-time zero error or benchmark classification results.
rows.check: The theorem and its conditions are accurately recorded, but its squared-loss convergence bound cannot determine any listed version's effect. It establishes exponential convergence toward zero as time tends to infinity, rather than finite-time zero classification error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
